In short, the feature encodes a learned decision about fine‐grained word or proper‑name segmentation in context.

direction_summaries.explanation: It appears that this feature is “marking” sub‐word splits—that is, it signals when a word (often a proper name, compound word, or common multi‐word phrase like “as well as”) should be segmented into its constituent pieces. In short, the feature encodes a learned decision about fine‐grained word or proper‑name segmentation in context.

direction_summaries.explanation: It appears that this feature is a punctuation‐boundary signal—in particular, one that fires strongly on terminal punctuation (usually a period) and “marks” the end of a sentence or clause so that the model treats the very next token (whether it’s a capital letter, a numeral, or other marker) differently. In short, it encodes a sentence‐boundary or list‐separator cue that influences how the token following a terminal punctuation is processed.

Removing the feature yields a contrapositive next token that no longer follows that announcement–style template.
